summary: For ages 9–11: teach the classic two-group dinosaur classification — Saurischia ('lizard-hipped') vs Ornithischia ('bird-hipped') — by sorting skeletons on a single diagnostic character, the direction the pubis bone points. Learners classify by evidence rather than memorising names, then confront the naming irony (birds descend from the LIZARD-hipped theropods, not the bird-hipped group) and meet the idea that the scheme itself was challenged in 2017, so a classification is a revisable hypothesis.
misconceptions: 'Birds came from the bird-hipped dinosaurs' — they came from lizard-hipped theropods; the backward pubis in birds is convergent.
'Meat-eaters are one hip group and plant-eaters the other' — sauropods (plant-eaters) are lizard-hipped alongside theropods.
'The hip name describes diet or size' — it describes pelvis anatomy only.
'Dinosaur classification is fixed and settled' — the traditional split has been actively challenged (Ornithoscelida).
'All bird-hipped dinosaurs are closely related to birds' — they are the group MORE distant from birds.

activities.title: Palaeontologist's hip-sorting table
steps: Examine each dinosaur's pelvis and trace which way the main shaft of the pubis bone points: forward-and-down, or swung backward alongside the ischium. (Some bird-hipped dinosaurs, such as Triceratops and duck-bills, also have a forward-pointing prepubic blade, so look for the backward shaft lying beside the ischium.)
Place each dinosaur into one of two bins: 'lizard-hipped' (Saurischia) or 'bird-hipped' (Ornithischia).
Sort a set that includes theropods (e.g. T. rex) AND sauropods (long-necks like Brachiosaurus) — both lizard-hipped — alongside Stegosaurus, Triceratops and duck-billed hadrosaurs — all bird-hipped.
As a final specimen, examine and classify a modern pigeon's pelvis, then check where it actually belongs in the evolutionary tree.
State in your own words the rule you used to decide each group.
activities.insight: In the classic two-group scheme, these dinosaurs can be sorted using one diagnostic anatomical character, the orientation of the pubis bone, not diet, size or overall appearance. Scientists also use many other characters. The group names describe hip shape, and the 'bird-hipped' label does NOT mean that group gave rise to birds. In fact birds are lizard-hipped theropods whose backward pubis evolved independently.

activities.title: Tap-to-reveal: two hips side by side
steps: Look at two labelled pelvis diagrams placed side by side: one with the pubis pointing forward/down, one with the pubis swung backward.
Tap each pubis to see its direction emphasised, then reveal the group name and example animals for that hip type.
Before revealing, predict the group name from the pubis direction alone.
activities.insight: In the classic scheme, the key feature taught for telling the two groups apart is the direction of the pubis bone. For typical members, each direction maps to a group name and a familiar set of examples, although some later lizard-hipped theropods (and birds) evolved a backward pubis.

activities.title: Why the family tree was re-argued
steps: Read or listen to a short account of why the two-group scheme was proposed and why a 2017 study (the Ornithoscelida hypothesis, Baron, Norman & Barrett) proposed reorganising it.
Compare a simple before/after family-tree sketch showing the traditional split and the proposed rearrangement.
Explain in one or two sentences why even a long-established classification can change when new evidence is weighed.
activities.insight: A classification is a hypothesis built from evidence, not a fixed fact; scientists actively debate and revise how dinosaurs are grouped.

activities.title: Check: naming trap and the sorting rule
steps: Answer: which group did birds evolve from — lizard-hipped or bird-hipped — and why is that surprising?
Sort several named species into Saurischia and Ornithischia.
Answer: what single feature do you look at to decide a dinosaur's group?
Explain: T. rex (a fierce meat-eater) and Brachiosaurus (a gentle long-neck) are in the SAME hip group — how can that be?
activities.insight: Secure understanding is shown by correctly classifying by hip structure AND explaining that the group names describe pelvis anatomy, not bird ancestry or diet.

checkQuestion: Dinosaurs are split into two groups by their hip bones: 'lizard-hipped' (Saurischia) and 'bird-hipped' (Ornithischia). Which group do you think birds evolved from — and why might that answer be surprising?
checkAnswer: Birds evolved from the LIZARD-hipped group (Saurischia — specifically theropods like T. rex), NOT the bird-hipped group, even though 'bird-hipped' sounds like it should be the bird ancestors. The two groups are defined by hip-bone structure, not by which became birds.
